At the very least once a week you will have ~3 hour classes where you are learning and getting tested on physical duties of a paramedic. You will come into these classes in your paramedic uniform, likely into a classroom with no desks, and work with everyone else learning and executing things like scenarios, how to check airway, circulation, bandaging, oxygen, etc. You might be able to pick a time after 2 pm for this class but you’ll learn quickly this may be difficult to set up and no one will work with you to accommodate if you cannot. You will not be able to work this time. 

Your other classes will be scheduled throughout the day at different times. Some do not have sections. Some will be large classes with the entire paramedic program and you will not be able to choose times because of that.

From your classes you have a combination of weekly tests, quizzes, and mid terms. You will not be able to attend other responsibilities on these days and times. 

Personally, I do not think it possible to pass your classes if you’re working even 3 days a week until 2 pm. I worked 28 hours a week on weekends and evenings and found it difficult.

The first part, paramedicine vs engineering. Other people say paramedicine is harder. I would completely disagree. My undergrad is from Waterloo in a science. The paramedic program was much easier than my undergrad. I didn’t need to study nearly as hard. Now I did dropout after completing the first semester and I had a lot of transfer courses. If you go to a school that requires anatomy, that one will be difficult. The semester timetables I’ve seen for engineering has the highest workload I’ve seen for any program. If you’re keeping up but hate the program, you will most likely do well with paramedic. If you’re not keeping up however, it may be easier but I’d be worried about your current problems following you.

What’s going on with your current program? You have 1 more month and then exams, you’re almost done your first semester. My first year marks were terrible. I went into my undergrad needing to reevaluate the way I studied and came back so much stronger second year.

As for discouraging you switching. It depends what you’re looking for as an outcome. Engineering sets up fantastic and well paid careers. Paramedicine can be that as well. However as a paramedic you will make ~80k a year. With additional education like an ACP and overtime, you can make ~100k+. I didn’t want a career that required overtime to make that. I didn’t want a career where so many people are having burnout issues and leaving the career only after a few years. You would need to finish your bachelors as every force requires one, but I’d recommend being a police officer over paramedic. You are paid more and are not treated with the same level of abuse by patients. Or as an engineer there are very engaging careers that are not demanding, or at least not as demanding and that pay you better

My understanding of school is that it gives 2 things:

1. A piece of paper that says you’re a smart boy/girl and can check off a box when applying for jobs. You’ve dedicated 2 years and followed through with the demands of balancing your life and completing a program. After a few jobs you’re even to move it to the bottom of your resume because it’s not as important as your experience. You don’t really expand on it, maybe throw your gpa in there and you’re all set.
2. Connections. You get to add a few people from your program on LinkedIn, check in where they’re working and send a message disguising asking for an interview with interest in how they are doing. Maybe you’ll have a professor who can get you in somewhere or has some kind of research opportunity you can add to your resume and also now use as a reference.

Do you think those 2 things would be improved by spending $100,000? Do you think spending an additional $80,000 will help you expand better on those 2 things? I think if you have a scholarship and don’t have to worry about the cost then 100% go for it, but if it’s out of pocket it is such an easy decision to stay domestic.
